A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GHBM/FedHBM work. Their complete main text and appendices are readable, and retained methods, experiments, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated-learning experiments on vision and language tasks, including accuracy, convergence and communication-cost results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds gradient-deviation measurements, synthetic regression results and comparisons between practical and theoretical algorithm variants.

M1.justification: The main momentum formulation remains, but v3 adds a distinct, evaluated theory variant using explicit past-gradient averaging and auxiliary server models (Algorithm 3; Figure 7). Displayed server aggregation changes from data-size weighting to uniform averaging. The shared/random initialization adaptations described in v2 Appendix C.6 are omitted.

E1.justification: The six principal vision and language datasets are retained. v3 adds a synthetic regression task for estimating quadratic-function coefficients (Figure 2; Appendix C.1), modestly extending task coverage.

E2.justification: FedACG and SCAFFOLD-M are added to the controlled CIFAR-100/Shakespeare comparison in v3 Table 2. FedACG also appears in the StackOverflow comparison in Figure 5. These evaluated comparators are absent from v2.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands the reported tuning grids for most baselines (v2 Table 6 versus v3 Table 7). GHBM's ResNet-20 local-learning-rate grid changes from {1, 0.5, 0.1} to {0.1, 0.01}. New experiments introduce cyclic-versus-full-participation controls and practical-versus-theory comparisons, while the initialization and learning-rate-decay protocols in v2 disappear.

E4.justification: v3 adds gradient-deviation diagnostics, a cyclic-participation convergence illustration, and practical-versus-theoretical implementation comparisons (Figures 1, 2 and 7). It removes v2's initialization/pretraining and learning-rate-scheduler studies, plus the detailed rounds-to-target analysis across heterogeneity levels. The existing tau sensitivity and final-accuracy-versus-heterogeneity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five independent runs and retain the same plus/minus accuracy reporting convention. No changed run-count policy, confidence-interval procedure or significance-testing practice is documented.

E6.justification: With revised tuning grids, several non-IID CIFAR-100 results change: ResNet-20 FedAvg goes from 21.9 to 24.7 and Mime from 9.0 to 26.8, while FedHBM remains 42.5 (v2 Table 1; v3 Table 2). Cost entries also change, including FedHBM/CNN communication from 3.9 to 5.2 GB. New comparator and diagnostic results accompany removal of several appendix result series.

T1.justification: v2 provides momentum identities and approximation bounds. v3 revises the error analysis and client-drift definition, then adds Theorem 4.11 and its convergence proof in Appendix B.4. The new result avoids bounded gradient dissimilarity under cyclic participation with tau = 1/C; Appendix B explicitly analyzes a separate theoretical algorithm.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add a central claim that generalized momentum alone enables convergence under arbitrary heterogeneity in cyclic partial participation, matching classical momentum's full-participation rate. v2 claims principled drift correction and empirical advantages without this convergence contribution.

C2.justification: v3 revises the mechanism explanation into noise, client-drift and gradient-lag components. It adds substantive qualifications about finite-sum versus streaming settings, cyclic participation, the lack of an explicit theoretical benefit from local steps, and differences between analyzed and practical algorithms. v2's dedicated broader-impact and extreme-scale limitations discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a public code URL instead of promising release after acceptance, revises parameter documentation and adds synthetic-data construction details. Most software, hardware and preprocessing information remains. Initialization/scheduler instructions disappear. The new regression client count is unresolved: Figure 2 states 10 clients, while Appendix C.1 states 50.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against Cheng et al. (2024), SCAFFOLD-M, FedACG, cyclic FedAvg and incremental gradient methods. Appendix A.1 adds discussion of ScaffNew, SPAM and second-order heterogeneity. These additions underpin a new novelty claim about momentum without variance reduction under cyclic partial participation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and existing method/theory narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Failure-case discussion moves from Section 5.4 to Appendix A.2, the standalone limitations section disappears, and the appendices are restructured. Author, affiliation and citation-style changes accompany this broader revision.

P2.justification: v3 adds a convergence-rate table and new diagnostic, cyclic-participation and algorithm-comparison graphics, while removing several appendix displays and revising benchmark curves. The retained tau and heterogeneity plots become Figures 3 and 4. Tables, algorithm boxes, highlighting and document layout are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline tuning and comparisons, code-access information, and the new convergence analysis with a practical/theoretical implementation comparison strengthen support and transparency. The net gain is limited by the theorem addressing a distinct variant and by removal of initialization and scheduler evidence. Reporting also becomes inconsistent: Section 5.3 retains gains of 20.6/14.4 points although revised Table 2 implies 17.8/12.1.
